rail_guard.text: York Station. The curve of the roof is famous, and it is one of the longest curved platforms in the country, so the trains seem to arrive politely round a corner.
Right, where to? We'll have you there before the tea goes cold.

c_legionette.text: A small spirit in a very old helmet stands to attention, and stands very correctly, for rather a long while. It seems to be waiting to be dismissed.

yrk_guide.text: Welcome to the Minster. The Great East Window has 311 panels and tells the story from Creation to the Apocalypse. The guide leaflet is 20 pages and the best part is the sandwiches.
There are 275 steps up the central tower. I've counted them for thirty years and they've never been the same number twice. They are, I promise you, medieval.

yrk_viking.text: The Vikings called York 'Jorvik'. In the Coppergate dig they found a Viking sock, knitted with a single needle in a technique called nålbinding. It's a bit holey, and 1,000 years old.

York had Romans, Vikings, Normans and railway barons. If you want to know why the street names end in 'gate', the Vikings' word for street was 'gata'. A 'bar' is a gate. A 'gate' is a street. It makes sense, when it's explained twice.

yrk_choc.text: York is chocolate city. Rowntree's and Terry's were both here. The KitKat came from York in 1935, and they still make them in a factory just down the road.
Terry's Chocolate Orange: tap it on the table, whack it, and the segments fall out. That's the York test. Nobody has ever failed it, but plenty have been stopped by the family.

yrk_rail.text: The National Railway Museum holds Mallard, the fastest steam locomotive in the world. In 1938 she reached 126 miles an hour, which is still the record, and the driver had a neat little bit of tweed on.
York was the railway capital of the north. Seven lines met here. Even now, you can't get anywhere in Britain without a change at York, as the saying goes.

yrk_ghost.text: York is the most haunted city in Europe, they say. I say there's a ghost on every street, and a ghost tour on every corner. A hundred and fifty haunted sites. And the same chap with a lantern in all of them.
The best ghost is the one you don't see. The second best is the one with a good gift shop.
